summary: Cover m9 fails gate C2 on one defect: all six waving hands have four digits (thumb and three fingers), not five. The top 30 percent is calm (yes). Margins are 590 px left and 653 px right, which keep every character well inside the frame (note). K1 has a defect: the line art has no nose. K2 and K3 are clean.

defects: All six raised waving hands have four digits: one thumb and three fingers. The fingers are spread, so the count is clear. A row scan of skin runs agrees: Ben rows 1826-1832 show three finger runs (600-629, 636-663, 670-692) and a thumb run at rows 1856-1862 (590-620); Sam row 1773 and May row 1818 also show three finger runs and one thumb run. The spec says "Count five digits on every open hand", and the brief says "five digits", which is not correct. The hands are small (about 100 px wide), so the count needs a close look; I record it as a defect because a child who counts the fingers of a waving hand counts four.
notes: Left margin 590 px and right margin 653 px. Both are about 15 percent of the width, far more than a 1 percent trim (40 px). No character touches the frame. The left margin is 50 px below the 640 px prompt target: this is a note, not a layout fault.

The six children agree with the approved sheets: Ben (3D, light-brown lumpy hair, light-blue T-shirt, blue trousers, gray sneakers), Mia (light-brown hair, pink bow, pink T-shirt, denim overalls, white shoes), Sam (brown side-swept hair, red T-shirt with white stripes, blue shorts, blue shoes), May (black hair, side ponytail, yellow star clip, yellow T-shirt, blue pleated skirt, white socks and sneakers), Pat (black hair with tufts, green T-shirt, brown shorts, brown sandals, no teddy bear), Nan (two buns with red ties, orange star T-shirt, red shorts, white sneakers).

Eyelash flicks: Pat and May show small flicks at the outer eye corners, and Mia also shows them. The approved cast sheet (ref2) shows the same flicks on Pat, May, and Mia. The flicks do not change the characters at book size. This is a note against the prompt only.
Nan shows a small dark tick at each outer eye corner. The Nan look sheet shows the same tick. This is a small mark.

Pip is whole, with floppy ears, a cream forehead stripe, a cream muzzle, a black nose, an open mouth, and a red collar with a gold tag. Two small pointed fur tufts show on the top of the head; the approved 3D Pip has the same tufts. They are not ears.
Pip seems to stand with straight front legs; the goal says he sits. His tail does not show from the front. These are notes.
The shoes have no clear contact shadow, so the children look a little raised above the floor. This is a note.
The lowered hand of each child is a smooth mitten, as on the approved sheets.
